jess: Heads-up — ran an nsys/perfetto trace against a production repro (multi-tenant batch workload). Seeing periodic 30–120ms tail stalls where GPU occupancy drops to 0 while we do a Triton/JIT-like compile + kernel selection. NVTX shows a KV-prefetch span right before the compile in most cases. Link: https://perfetto.dev/trace?token=REDACTED (nsys output attached)
vikram: Can you paste the nsys invocation and a tiny flame excerpt? trying to repro locally :eyes:
jess: Command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,os --output=/tmp/trace_1805 --sample=cpu,ticks --duration=60s
```
Flame excerpt (high level):
- KV_PREFETCH (NVTX span) — 18–35ms
- compile_and_link_kernels() — 40–110ms
- GPU idle / CU queue drain — 20–40ms
nvtx shows prefetch often touching ~200MB of serialized kernels right before compile.
nikhil: Interesting. Two hypothesis: (1) KV-prefetch is preloading a different model variant/quantization path that invalidates kernels or clobbers cache, causing Triton to recompile; (2) our compile-worker thread pool is serialized by a lock held during prefetch. Either could cause short bursts of “compile backpressure”.
carmen: I pulled the histograms for the same run — 1200 total compiles, 98th = 93ms, 99.5th = 210ms. When I disabled KV-prefetch in a dogfood cluster (quick toggle), 99.5th drops to 58ms but average token latency goes up by ~3.2% (likely cache miss on runtime kernels).
perf-bot: auto-analysis: compile_spike_count=18; avg_compile_ms=34; tail_99_9_compile_ms=210; correlated_kv_prefetch=true
vikram: Good signal. Next steps I propose:
- add NVTX spans around compile queue enqueuing and kernel cache lookup
- instrument compile-worker lock contention (perf counters / eBPF)
- run isolated repro with small model + synthetic batching to narrow root cause
jess: I'll add spans and run focused nsys with `--sample=cpu,threads` for lock contention. Schedule: will run tonight and post traces.
nikhil: I also have a quick patch we can try: short-circuit KV-prefetch for batch_size >= 32 or seq_len <= 64 (heuristic). Pseudocode:
```
if (batch_size >= 32 || seq_len <= 64) {
  skip_kv_prefetch();
} else {
  prefetch_kv();
}
```
This reduced compile correlation in a small A/B test.
carmen: Also worth testing changing compile-parallelism from 1 -> 4 (env var TRITON_COMPILE_THREADS). Might hide latency but could increase CPU/memory pressure.
vikram: One caution — if compile just shifts and multiple compiles run concurrently, it may increase total tail if kernel cache evictions happen. We need per-GPU kernel cache metrics (entries, hits, evictions).
jess: Agreed. I'll include kernel-cache nvprof counters and add a perfetto slice for kernel cache ops. If results look reproducible, we should consider a conservative default change (disable prefetch for short-seqs) and add a metric gate in the console.
carmen: Filing a revert candidate for the kernel-cache allocator change from 2026-02-14 just in case — linking in the PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/PR-1234
nikhil: I'll run microbenchmarks toggling `KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED` + TRITON_COMPILE_THREADS and dump compile latency CCDFs.
jess: Thanks — assignments: jess (traces + nvtx spans), vikram (lock/eBPF instrumentation), nikhil (A/B microbench + patch), carmen (PR/revert readiness). Will report back tomorrow. :thumbsup:
vikram: Thanks — if anyone gets a quick repro, ping #eng-runtime and drop the synthetic trace, happy to help correlate.
